**7th May 2556, 1921 hours**

**Unknown planet, surface**

Stan had left the ramp down as he stepped out into the clearing, the once vibrant forest had lost most of it's luster and was largely a patchy mess of grass and trees. There had been a beacon here, an ancient landing signal that responded to his call and beckoned him to come down. That seemed to raise more questions without answering any question, as far as the beacon knew the query for more information was just background chatter. Finding it was easier said than done too, the damned thing had been half buried by a landside and his pocket computer's geiger counter went wild when he got too close.

Looking around he found the remains of a village, the native inhabitants were long, long gone. What remained was the stone foundations, half-buried and barely recognizable, centuries of a war with the local ecosystem took it's toll. Stan had seen this before, a world completely pulverized by his kind who had become quite used to scorching entire worlds in the face of better-equipped and more advanced enemies to force them to leave humanity alone. That was part of the reason why his adopted nation, based on a forgotten world called Seylonis, had left the wider empire that humanity had built. They wanted nothing of the brewing war, of wrecked worlds and ruined peoples, fascism and strife wrought by human hands.

Jade and Inzili stepped out on to the surface carefully, their bundled up toddlers following close behind in their cute little boots and overalls that looked just like their father's own clothes, except he had a worn leather jacket that had lost it's sleeves and all that remained was a makeshift vest.

"Stay close, little ones," Inzili hissed, her nose up to the breeze as she sniffed.

Her brain searched deep in her memory, it knew that scent, all those odors from a time long before, but she couldn't place it... what was it? Her head shook to clear the wondering, her eyes scanning the unfamiliar horizon as she led her children from the safety of the ship out to where Stan was kneeling.

"Dunno, but whatever happened here happened a real long time ago," he said, digging out a worn chunk of metal from the soil with a knife. After a few more seconds of effort he peeled it up, "huh, lookit this... fuckin' Corporate Wars shit."

Stan turned it over to look, it seemed like some sort of hydraulic device with circuitry probably for controlling it, but Inzili couldn't be sure.

"This here is an old actuator controller for an autocannon, the service tag's still on... shit, this went out of action in twenty-three thirty seven. Or at least that's when she was last serviced," as he finished he looked up at her, grinning slightly. Stan clearly loved picking through old wrecks, it seemed so natural to him.

"You are good with junk, you know this?" she grinned with amusement.

Jade folded her arms across her chest and shook her head. "No, he's good at looking at crap as old as he is. Sometimes fixing it."

"Hey! Them's fightin' words," he replied with mock outrage. "I keep that ship flyin' mighty fine, don't I?"

"Honey, when you smarten up and get us a *real* ship I'll be impressed."

Real ship? Inzili had no interest in their playful bickering, their ship served them well enough; it was the people inside who made it a home. Her home! A much better pursuit than whatever devices he had found, they were all junk now as was this world, a broken mess ruined by some human war over some human dispute.

"I don't care what ship we fly, where are we?" she asked, looking around. "What world is this?"

Whoever lived on this world so long ago suffered because of Stan's kind and for a brief moment she almost resented him for that. Without a doubt she absolutely hated humans, those damned smooth-skinned apes knew only destruction and exploitation, such bitterly cruel creatures! Except for Stan of course, he was... different; or at least that's what she told herself. Sometimes when he spoke of his past it wasn't easy to listen, and even then she suspected he only revealed what he felt she could stomach.

"Sweetheart, I ain't got the fuckin' foggiest idea. I thought this place was uncharted but that beacon over yonder there is proof positive otherwise."

"'Over yonder...'" Jade giggled.

Stan glared at her and shook his head. "Don't make fun of how I talk, I grew up in a shipbreaker village. We weren't fancy folk."

Standing up he looked around, his eyes trying to peer through the haze in the distance that had surely been introduced when the world was being strip-mined of it's valuables. He passed the wrecked actuator over to Jade to keep her occupied, looking past her at his landed ship and the top turret slowly rotating as it scanned the sky for threats. Of course the possibility anyone would show up would be almost nonexistent but he was still cautious and liked to be prepared. Meanwhile the bottom turret remained in it's unlocked but forward-facing position, those twin cannons designed specifically for punching holes in ship armor would be overkill against local wildlife.

Both the toddlers had transitioned from clinging to Jade to clinging onto Stan's jumpsuit with their tiny fists as they looked around the very big and very, very scary world. They had never seen natural sunlight or been on a planet, their world was the tiny confines of Stan's ship which didn't have grass, dirt, sun, or sky or all the birds, bugs, and animals that lived and died on this alien world. On occasion little Nuva would turn her nose up to the wind and snort in the breeze, her cheeks puffing out as she huffed the used air out her mouth to keep her nostrils clean. She didn't dare to leave her father's leg though, and as he slowly walked they waddled after to keep that wad of fabric in their grip.

Suddenly Nuva perked up and warbled an alarm, an instinctive "auu-waa" that sounded a lot like something that would come out of a bird. Inzili's scales bristled at the noise, her eyes darting around to find her child.

Stan undid his holster and put his hand on the large-bore pistol he always had at his side when he was out and about. "Yeah sweetheart, daddy heard it too," he murmured, his eyes sharp on the treeline but his head didn't turn and his pace didn't change.

Inzili was not as discreet, she was looking around to spot any danger, her gaze had shifted from looking forward and focused on specific objects to a more panoramic view, an advantage she had over Stan. Even so she couldn't locate the source of her daughter's distress, but the change in wind made her nostrils flare at the musky odor.

She noticed Stan had changed directions and started making a wide circle around the ship but it was too late, their pursuers were already moving through the bush and closing to attack. Nuva barked and hid on the other side of Stan's leg, huddled close to her sister and with her back to her mother's leg. Hearing her daughter's distress set off all sorts of hormonal responses in Inzili, who bristled as she watched the figures moving through the dense grasses but within the cover of the trees.

"Backwards ladies, back up to the ship," Stan said calmly, his voice firm as iron. "Right now. Get the kids and go."

Since he knew they knew he could see them he brought out his sidearm and kept it in front of him, both hands on the grip as he steadied himself to start dropping anyone who got close. Inzili scooped up both the tiny lizards and moved backwards with Stan, every step careful and measured as the figures fanned out and snuck low through the grass. Jade was already back at the ship, just as Stan had told her to do in this sort of situation, but he had never expected to have his family with him.

"Y'all best fuck right off, that's mighty close enough!" he called out to them, stopping to stand on a small mound that gave him a height advantage.

Inzili kept moving, and when it was clear Stan wasn't retreating she ran at full pace.

"Last fuckin' warning," he called out, a thick thumb pulling back the hammer.

Stan didn't hesitate the moment one of them crossed the invisible boundary he had marked in the grassy field. At first he warned the intruder with a single shot past it's head, then as it approached further he gave it another on the other side which only seemed to provoke it. When the figure raised up he saw it was a tall, muscular female lizard that gave a mighty war cry before charging forward. Feeling merciful Stan flicked a switch on his trusty weapon and squeezed the trigger.

There seemed to be the smallest of delays from the time he pulled the trigger to the moment the warrior got a rubber slug right in the middle of her chest. His aim was perfect, and the shot instantly dropped her.

She gasped and hacked, her claws digging into her scales as she fought to catch her breath. Stan took a few steps forward, popping off another round at another one who stood up, but this time it was not a relatively soft rubber round. Instead the top of her shield exploded into tiny pieces, and the lizard let out a startled snarl as she slinked back.
